insights.methodology: Every insight cites the specific ratio/period pair it is derived from in ratios_timeseries.json.

risk_signals.statement: NPL ratio jumped from 5.22% (FY2011) to a peak of 8.42% (FY2012) and stayed in an 8%+ range through FY2015, then ground down slowly through the rest of the decade to a low of 6.33% (FY2018) before a mid-cycle bump back to 7.81% in FY2019 - a persistently elevated but non-worsening asset-quality profile rather than a sharp deterioration.

From FY2019's 7.81% local peak, NPL ratio declined nearly every year through FY2025, reaching a series-low 4.84% - a sustained six-year improvement in asset quality even as total assets nearly doubled (193.2bn to 321.4bn) over the same span.

ROE rose from 11.09% (FY2021) to 19.23% (FY2025) and ROA from 0.85% to 1.86% over the same span, with the sharpest single-year jump in FY2024 (ROA 1.22% -> 1.74%, ROE 14.12% -> 18.43%) coinciding with FY2024's Gross Income growth of roughly 30% year-on-year - the strongest profitability stretch in the bank's 15-year public history, sustained (not reversed) into FY2025.

Newly backfilled Q1-Q3 interim data (2013-2025, 30 quarters, ratios_timeseries.json) shows FY2024's profitability jump was not a single strong Q4 -- annualized ROE climbed sequentially every quarter that year: 9.92% (Q1) -> 16.83% (Q2) -> 17.21% (Q3) -> 18.43% (Q4), a roughly 8.5-percentage-point Q1-to-Q4 spread, the largest intra-year acceleration in the newly visible 2020-2025 interim series. By contrast FY2021 (9.33% -> 11.09%, a 1.8pp spread) and FY2022 (9.11% Q1, peaking mid-year at 14.94% in Q2 before easing to 13.27% by Q4) show flatter or non-monotonic intra-year patterns, so FY2024 is a genuine acceleration in the bank's underlying quarterly earnings trajectory, not a year-end-only effect (e.g. a one-off provision release or bonus).

insights.historical_context: Uttara Bank's 15-year public history shows a bank that spent the first decade (FY2011-FY2019) working through an elevated but stable 6-8% NPL ratio while growing at a moderate pace, then entered a sustained improvement phase from FY2019 onward: NPL ratio nearly halved by FY2025 (7.81% to 4.84%) while total assets more than tripled since FY2015 (151.5bn to 321.4bn) and profitability metrics (ROA, ROE) reached series highs in FY2024-FY2025. There is no year in the series showing a sharp asset-quality shock; the pattern throughout is gradual, not cyclical.
